article_content: The trial of Dr. Kermit Gosnell, a Philadelphia abortion provider, has entered its fourth day of jury deliberations. The jurors have requested a description of the babies at the center of the case, in which Gosnell is accused of using scissors to sever their spinal cords. According to prosecutors, some of the infants were born alive and viable during the sixth, seventh, and eighth months of pregnancy. In the state of Pennsylvania, abortions are only permitted after 24 weeks if the mother's health is at risk. The jury has also asked for a written definition of RICO charges and a property receipt for the medications seized from the clinic and entered into evidence. RICO charges stem from the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act. Following consultation with attorneys, Judge Jeffrey Minehart addressed the jury's inquiries in the deliberation room. Gosnell and his co-defendant, Eileen O'Neill, were not present in the courtroom. The nature of the questions suggests that the jury has completed its review of the charges against O'Neill, who is accused of practicing without a license, and has moved on to considering the case against Gosnell. If found guilty of first-degree murder, Gosnell, who is not certified as an obstetrician or gynecologist, could face the death penalty. The defense argues that the infants were already deceased, and Gosnell provided necessary healthcare services to low-income patients.
